![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100385/assets/47c1bc45869431b7e834f1f6a4d91f2f40b77e2ec44af058882dcb5e670cc07d.png)

If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $x=y,\,$ $x=9-2y,$ and the lines $y=1,$ and $y=3,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type II region. To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100385/assets/7f97a7bd9e722440e1fd7bfe1a7293f989928275cd9b88369aa5650bce1037dd.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,y\le x\le 9-2y}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{y}^{9-2y}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[{\int }_{y}^{9-2y}f(x,y)\,dx]dy\end{aligned}
$$
